solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sees hint about locations where drivers may pull in

definitions.text: locations where drivers may pull in

indicators.note: to bring something about is to turn it round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to spot something is to see it
a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: Someone spots a hint about good places for motorists to pull over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' sits between the two parts and looks like 'concerning', but it turns the whole sequence round, not just the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing cars pull into the pits for fuel and tyres, and road travellers also take breaks at roadside stopping places.

clue.text: Astronaut, first to last, nags

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front to the end of the word

blocks.note: a jocular word for someone who travels in space

explanation.surface: An astronaut is pestered by complaints from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nags' looks like a verb meaning pesters, but it is the plural noun for horses; a pacer is a horse that paces, often used in harness racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nag is an informal word for a horse, and pacers are horses trained to a particular gait.

clue.text: Secret society joined by a new islander

blocks.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A secret society admits a newcomer from some island.
explanation.walkthrough: A tong is a Chinese secret society or gang, a term often met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom, so a native of it is a Pacific islander.

clue.text: Rather unpleasant fellow, say, always turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning upward means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a toad is a loathsome person
e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A rather nasty man keeps popping up wherever you go.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last piece is turned; 'say' is the usual crossword signal for EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as qualifying adverbs meaning somewhat or fairly, as in 'to a degree tired' or 'rather tired'.

clue.text: Shrewdness a star’s shown when joining urban community

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a day', meaning per
Spica is the brightest star in Virgo
a city is an urban community

explanation.surface: A celebrity shows good sense by settling in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'a' does real work: it means 'each', as in 'twice a week', which is PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacity is keen insight or discernment, the quality of sharp judgement also called shrewdness.

clue.text: Prevent what allows youngster to fall asleep in school

indicators.note: placing one thing within another puts it inside the other's letters

blocks.clueFragment: what allows youngster to fall asleep
blocks.note: a baby's bed
SCH is an abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school puts a stop to children napping in class.
explanation.walkthrough: A cot is a baby's bed with high sides (a crib in American English).
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan or rumour is to put an end to it, so it means to stop or thwart something.

clue.text: It’s right in church to perform part of service in Latin

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
CE is the Church of England
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is proper to sing part of the Mass in Latin in church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is the standard crossword church; R goes inside it before DO is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creed of the Mass begins with this Latin word meaning 'I believe', and gives its name to that section of the liturgy.

clue.text: Philosophers? Most of that lot maybe fret inwardly

indicators.note: most of something is all but a small part, so the final letter goes
something held inwardly is placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: a way of pointing at a group of things
a fret is a sea mist on the east coast of Britain; 'maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Are these philosophers, perhaps worrying privately?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like the verb to worry, but here it is a sea fret, a coastal fog, so it is one example of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomists are followers of the philosophy and theology of Thomas Aquinas, so they form a school of thinkers.

clue.text: Carriers conveying small ancestors of ours?

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
mini means small

explanation.surface: Something carrying tiny forebears of the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: hominids include our forebears but also living great apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominids are the primate family that includes humans and our extinct evolutionary forerunners.

clue.text: Period of time in which to embed a plant

indicators.note: embedding something in another sets it inside, so the outer word is split around it

blocks.note: a hundred years
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to set a plant into some era, like a time capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads like a verb (to plant something), but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaury is a small flowering herb of the gentian family, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Margaret with expression of surprise — maiden showing a lot of resistance

blocks.note: Meg is a short form of Margaret
an exclamation of surprise
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A surprised girl named Margaret puts up a stubborn fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, written M on the scoresheet. 'Resistance' is electrical, not personal.
explanation.definitionFit: A megohm is a million ohms, the unit of electrical resistance, so it is a large quantity of it.

clue.text: Companies not fussed about providing payment for injury?

indicators.note: something fussed about is bustled and messed around, so the order is disturbed

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Businesses that shrug off paying damages to people they have hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fussed' reads as 'unconcerned', but 'not' belongs with the letters and 'fussed about' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded to someone for loss or harm suffered is called compensation, as in a damages claim after an accident.

clue.text: Studied English to become an author

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone took an English degree in order to become a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'read' a subject at university, meaning study it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, best known for The Cloister and the Hearth, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Step up, being against standing still

definitions.note: a phrase read as PRO MOTION, being in favour of movement

blocks.note: first meaning: a rise in rank at work
second meaning, split in two: in favour of moving

explanation.surface: An exhortation to get moving, because standing still is not an option.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: someone against standing still is for movement, which splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is an advance to a higher job or rank, which people also call a step up the ladder.

clue.text: Hurried down at first and fell

blocks.note: first meaning: hastened, brought on suddenly, as a crisis may be
second meaning: came down as rain or snow, or dropped out of a solution

explanation.surface: Someone rushed downstairs at the start and took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down at first' hints at the word's original sense, to throw down headlong, before it came to mean hasten; the two definitions sit either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To precipitate events is to hasten them, and rain or a chemical solid that precipitates comes down or settles out.

clue.text: Man has a dig to get round plant

blocks.note: a tom is a male, especially a male cat
taken as written
to till the soil is to dig it
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A gardener digs around a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get round' looks like an instruction to put letters around something, but 'round' is simply the letter O added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a Mexican plant of the nightshade family grown for its small husked fruit used in salsas.

clue.text: It could suggest I step where one may slither dangerously?

indicators.note: the answer is read as a clue in its own right, with its first word the signal to rearrange

blocks.note: in the answer read as a clue, this word is what says the letters go astray
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A skier warns that one false step here could send them sliding into danger.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as a clue, and OFF is a signal to rearrange PISTE, which gives back 'I step'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from the prepared, marked runs, on ungroomed snow, is risky because of avalanches and hidden hazards.

clue.text: Music-maker having wine outside home

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
one piece sits on the outside of the other, wrapping round it

blocks.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A musician drinks wine outside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music-maker' suggests a person, but it is an instrument. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, so it is an object that produces music rather than a person.

clue.text: Unwise financial procedure that could have company in money, strangely

indicators.note: something strange is out of the normal order, so the letters are jumbled
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: read the answer as a clue: this first word is a jumbling signal, matching this adverb
taken letter for letter
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A costly business mistake: bringing a company into money matters in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as a clue, would produce the wordplay phrase, with its first word acting as the jumbling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A false economy is a saving that ends up costing more, such as buying cheap goods that soon need replacing.

clue.text: Regal request?

definitions.note: read as AS KING, like a monarch

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: in the manner of a monarch
second meaning: making a request

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after two letters to get the royal meaning; the question mark warns of the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking is the act of making a request, while the two-word phrase describes behaving like a monarch.

clue.text: Plasterwork that is what you expect to obtain

blocks.note: par is the normal or expected standard
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Plastering that turns out exactly as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: Par is the expected score on a golf hole, hence the standard you expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Parget is ornamental plaster, often moulded in patterns on the outside walls of old East Anglian houses.

clue.text: Report can supply just the opposite

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new shape

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A news report is able to provide the exact reverse of the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb 'provide', but it is the adverb from supple, pronounced 'supple-ee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Per contra is a Latin phrase meaning on the other hand or on the contrary, used to introduce an opposing point.

clue.text: Indication of what’s hot or cold may be here, readily available

definitions.text: Indication of what’s hot or cold may be here

blocks.clueFragment: Indication of what’s hot or cold may be here
blocks.note: first meaning: where H or C labels are printed on a bathroom fitting
second meaning: ready to use whenever wanted

explanation.surface: A label showing hot or cold can be found somewhere handy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic description: the H and C that mark hot and cold water are found on a tap (a faucet).
explanation.definitionFit: Beer drawn from a barrel is served on draught, hence the idiom for anything instantly and easily obtainable.

clue.text: Falsetto’s cast in part in opera

indicators.note: only a portion of the words is used, a run of letters sitting within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A male falsetto singer has been given a role in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as being chosen for a role, fitting the opera picture, but it just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera about a singer, her painter lover and the villainous police chief Scarpia.

clue.text: Body of legislators had to back second measure

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an en is a printer's measure of width
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Lawmakers had to support a second bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests reversal, but ATE is not turned round; it simply stands behind the other two pieces. 'Measure' looks like a bill, but it is the printer's en.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, such as the upper house of the US Congress.

clue.text: Dealing with famous author

blocks.note: first meaning: handling, as with questions
second meaning: the eighteenth-century novelist Henry

explanation.surface: Handling a well-known writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones; the first sense comes from cricket, where fielders deal with the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielding questions means handling them as they come, and Henry Fielding is a celebrated English novelist.

clue.text: Shocking treatment you guards quietly copy

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: electroconvulsive therapy
ye is the old form of you
p (piano) is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: An electric shock treatment protects you by quietly imitating something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like 'appalling' but is literal: ECT is electric shock therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectype is a reproduction of an original, as opposed to the prototype, so it is a duplicate.

clue.text: Go hunt, us? Quite otherwise, if something’s this

definitions.text: Go hunt, us? Quite otherwise, if something’s this

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters take another arrangement

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Should we go hunting for it? Not at all, if nobody wants it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: something nobody looks for is the opposite of what we go hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not looked for or requested, like unsought advice, is the reverse of a thing people actively pursue.
